effect_floor_reason: Declared after numerical preflight and before any composed margin is read. The predeclared rule is: keep 1e-8 when the worst reference numerical gap is below 1e-10. Do not use scientific |I| or G magnitudes to move the floor. Reference systems are the unconstrained baseline, a continuous multiplier at the named W4 factors, m = 0 against a named prohibit rule, and the v0.6 prohibit/prohibit anchor singleton. Maximum block-versus-dense landing gap: 1.3877787807814457e-17. Maximum block-versus-dense committor gap: 4.440892098500626e-16. Maximum direct-versus-iterative committor gap: 1.5237811012980274e-14, on the m = 0 kernel. Anchor singleton versus the published Generation 6 Delta_T: 0.0. Unconditional control triad spread stays below 1e-8. Worst of those gaps: 1.5237811012980274e-14, which is below 1e-10, so the floor stays 1e-8. Composed margins were not an input. Float64 solutions are not exact. The floor is not retuned after the census.
match_tolerance_reason: The matching tolerance is not the scientific effect floor. The same numerical preflight supports an absolute singleton tolerance of 1e-8, because the worst reference gap 1.5237811012980274e-14 is below 1e-10. An earlier joint residual just above 1e-8 on the weak_suppress erasure was a golden-section stop at log10 width 1e-4. After the stop was tightened to 1e-7, that joint residual fell below 1e-8. The tolerance was not loosened. It is not retuned after composed margins are read.
joint_scale_floor_reason: Separate from match_tolerance and from effect_floor. Each direction's scale is max(|Delta_T|, 1e-8). If both |Delta_T| are below 1e-8, the scale source is the baseline committor, max(|Q0|, 1e-8). Scales are functions of the target only. They are not adjusted to improve a match.
